newsitem.title: USA: Man admits defrauding insurers of $17 million.
newsitem.headline: Man admits defrauding insurers of $17 million.

text.p: A New York man has pleaded guilty to defrauding five major insurance companies of $17 million by obtaining low-cost group medical insurance based on bogus information, federal prosecutors said Tuesday.
Solomon Sprei, 42, of Brooklyn pleaded guilty in Manhattan federal court on Monday to one count of mail fraud conspiracy and one count of wire fraud conspiracy.
Sprei admitting obtaining the insurance through misrepresentations as to who would be covered by the insurance and by providing fraudulent claims and premium experience for the group.
The defrauded companies are Empire Blue Cross and Blue Shield, CNA Insurance Cos., State Mutual Life Assurance Co. of America, The Traveler's Co. and Prudential Insurance Co. of America.
Sprei faces a possible maximum sentence of 10 years in prison and a $500,000 fine.

Among charges against Sprei was that he obtained low-cost group medical insurance from Empire Blue Cross and Blue Shield on the pretense that the insurance would be used to cover the health costs of members of a labour union with a history of low expenditures.
Rather than applying the coverage to union members, he sold it for profit to thousands of members of the public without regard to their union affiliation, employment or health.
